source.title: Scaling Language-Centric Omnimodal Representation Learning
source.authors: Chenghao Xiao; Hou Pong Chan; Hao Zhang; Weiwen Xu; Mahani Aljunied; Yu Rong

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies a different relationship—multimodal representation performance after contrastive learning versus generative capability—not the stated loss-scaling laws or their compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The text-only CL geometry analyses and benchmark comparisons do not measure the claim’s loss-scaling behavior. The paper’s own GRSL results and SeaDoc retrieval results concern related, but different, representation-generation relationships; they are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The paper's 'Generation-Representation Scaling Law' is a positive cross-backbone correlation between generative benchmark scores and post-contrastive embedding scores, across 2–5 MLLMs. It reports no pretraining loss, no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute, no extrapolation, no compute-optimal allocation and no shape sweep. Its 3B vs 7B comparisons (Tables 1 and 3, Figure 2) use only two sizes per family, with no fitted trend, so they do not test V6 as stated. 'Scaling law' is used in name only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim generative pretraining, not cross-modal data volume, is the central driver of multimodal representation learning. They support the GRSL with a PAC-Bayesian bound in which lower generative loss tightens the bound on contrastive risk. The empirical 'law' is a positive correlation across a handful of backbones, not a fitted functional form.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a generation-representation relationship for multimodal embeddings, rather than measuring held-out language-model loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: SeaDoc retrieval results vary with resolution and continual-SFT data composition. The appendix also reports task-dependent sensitivity to LoRA rank and alpha, including loss spikes at rank 256 and alpha 512.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-CL embedding performance correlates positively with pre-CL generative benchmark performance across backbones (OCR image-text, video-text, audio-text). Shown in figures only, with no coefficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastively refined MLLM embedding quality increases with the backbone's generative benchmark performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On SeaDoc, continual SFT on OCR-only data before CL collapses retrieval at low resolution; high resolution partly mitigates this, and adding PixmoCaps improves retrieval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of continual generative SFT for later embedding quality depends on resolution and data mix.

fits_no_version.finding: Within Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen2.5-Omni, the 7B variants beat the 3B variants on MIEB-Lite and MIEB-Sub18 after the same CL (e.g., Table 3 LoRA average 71.98 vs 66.28). Only two sizes, no fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger MLLM backbones yield better embeddings after identical lightweight CL.

record.problems: Figure 6 reports the positive relationships visually without numerical correlation coefficients or uncertainty estimates; the plotted cross-backbone sample is small. Figure 7 retrieval values are presented only in the figure, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying loss-scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal-allocation, or architecture-shape results were reported. Geometry analyses and general benchmark comparisons were omitted because they do not measure the claim’s stated behaviors.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No compute-optimal parameter or token allocation.
No depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count. The kernel alignment figure notes the 3B model has more layers than the 7B, but parameter count is not held fixed.
No power-law fit for multimodal or fine-tuning regimes. The GRSL is a correlation between benchmark scores, not a loss power law.
Downstream embedding scores are compared only at 3B vs 7B, with no scale trend or relation to pretraining loss. The GRSL relates downstream scores to other downstream scores.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal split are examined.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is kept: none of V1–V7 is tested. The model-size comparison is at most a two-point observation on embedding benchmarks and is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a V6 test.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fit on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effect of depth, width, and other architecture details on loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes.
The study relates downstream representation scores to generative benchmark performance, not to model scale or pretraining loss as specified in this version.
Dependence of the stated loss-scaling exponents or compute-optimal split on setup or fitting choices.
